title: The Sign of Jonah
notes: This chunk delivers dense scene-by-scene typology of Jonah against the Passion, with clear internal symbol work on heart of the earth/seas and the great fish as kingdom. Prevalence tables and the refusal of the three-days-only reading fit the book’s method. Residual house-style defects cluster in multiple And/But sentence opens and director cues (listen, mark, Notice, hold). One high-severity grammar break appears in the Rome/Jerusalem mount sentence, where the subject collapses after the final em-dash. Surgical fixes restore the And/But ban and the broken clause without touching doctrine or quoted scripture.

The chunk’s strength is its dense, law-positive chaining of Jonah to the Passion and the nations, capped by a clean scene-by-scene table and a sharp correction of Augustine’s two-frame compression. The recovery claim is assertive and the symbol work (belly/Sheol, reeds/suph, yeshuah, great city) stays tight. Residual problems are concentrated in presenter staging: multiple “Now/Listen/See/Step back/mark here” director cues, three author-prose sentence opens with And/But/That, and second-person “you have just watched/hold/read” framing that softens the assertiveness. A few register slips (“reward the dig,” “no skeptic would script”) also surface. Surgical cuts restore the author’s voice without touching doctrine or quoted text.

proposals.old: But listen to how Luke reports the same saying:
proposals.summary: Remove banned But open and staging cue listen.
proposals.rationale: Author prose may not start with But; listen functions as a director cue barred by house style.

proposals.old: But Scripture itself locates the heart of the earth.
proposals.new: Scripture itself locates the heart of the earth.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences that begin with But.

proposals.old: And the world Jesus spoke into knew the name: Philo of Alexandria calls Jerusalem the __“heart of the whole earth”__; the Sibylline Oracles, __“the navel and heart of the earth”__; later Greek copies of Ezekiel even change __“navel”__ to __“heart”__ where Jerusalem is in view.
proposals.new: The world Jesus spoke into knew the name: Philo of Alexandria calls Jerusalem the __“heart of the whole earth”__; the Sibylline Oracles, __“the navel and heart of the earth”__; later Greek copies of Ezekiel even change __“navel”__ to __“heart”__ where Jerusalem is in view.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences that begin with And.

proposals.old: And with that phrase the proof closes inside Scripture itself.
proposals.new: With that phrase the proof closes inside Scripture itself.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences that begin with And.

proposals.old: And they wash their hands of him — the sailors in words, __“lay not upon us innocent blood”__ (Jonah 1:14); the governor in water, __“I am innocent of the blood of this just person”__ (Matthew 27:24).
proposals.new: They wash their hands of him — the sailors in words, __“lay not upon us innocent blood”__ (Jonah 1:14); the governor in water, __“I am innocent of the blood of this just person”__ (Matthew 27:24).
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences that begin with And.

proposals.old: And mark the double truth in the verbs: Jonah offers himself — __“cast me forth”__ — yet it is other hands that take him up and cast him; exactly as the Messiah is __“delivered… by wicked hands”__ (Acts 2:23) and yet insists, __“No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself”__ (John 10:18).
proposals.new: The verbs carry a double truth: Jonah offers himself — __“cast me forth”__ — yet it is other hands that take him up and cast him; exactly as the Messiah is __“delivered… by wicked hands”__ (Acts 2:23) and yet insists, __“No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself”__ (John 10:18).
proposals.summary: Remove And open and director cue mark.
proposals.rationale: Banned And start plus Mark that-style staging; rewrite asserts the same claim without either.

proposals.old: Notice also who sends it: __“the LORD had *prepared* a sym:sym-fish-2[great fish]”__ (Jonah 1:17) — _vayman_, appointed.
proposals.new: Who sends it is named: __“the LORD had *prepared* a sym:sym-fish-2[great fish]”__ (Jonah 1:17) — _vayman_, appointed.
proposals.rationale: Notice that is an explicit house-style director cue; the replacement keeps the claim and the quote intact.

proposals.old: Rome is the *iron* of Nebuchadnezzar’s image — Daniel named the second and third kingdoms outright, Medo-Persia and Greece (Daniel 8:20-21), and the iron fourth that __“breaketh in pieces”__ all before it (Daniel 2:40) is the empire that held the world when He came — the current face of the one world-empire, and offered her true King she chose her mount instead: __“We have no king but Caesar”__ (John 19:15).
proposals.new: Rome is the *iron* of Nebuchadnezzar’s image — Daniel named the second and third kingdoms outright, Medo-Persia and Greece (Daniel 8:20-21), and the iron fourth that __“breaketh in pieces”__ all before it (Daniel 2:40) is the empire that held the world when He came — the current face of the one world-empire. Offered her true King, she chose her mount instead: __“We have no king but Caesar”__ (John 19:15).
proposals.summary: Repair subject collapse after the final em-dash.
proposals.rationale: The clause and offered her true King she chose her mount instead loses its subject and becomes a fragment; a clean sentence break restores grammar while preserving the claim.

proposals.old: And he is __“brought up… from corruption”__ — the precise word Peter presses at Pentecost: __“thou wilt not… suffer thine Holy One to see corruption”__ (Psalm 16:10; Acts 2:27).
proposals.new: He is __“brought up… from corruption”__ — the precise word Peter presses at Pentecost: __“thou wilt not… suffer thine Holy One to see corruption”__ (Psalm 16:10; Acts 2:27).
proposals.summary: Remove banned author-prose sentence open with And.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids sentences in author prose starting with And. Dropping the conjunction keeps the claim intact and denser.

proposals.old: Two details of the prayer reward the dig.
proposals.new: Two details of the prayer repay close reading.
proposals.summary: Replace informal “reward the dig” register slip.
proposals.rationale: “Reward the dig” is presenter slang that undercuts the book’s density. The replacement keeps the same force without the colloquial turn.

proposals.old: Now set the two castings side by side, because the contrast is the verdict.
proposals.new: Set the two castings side by side: the contrast is the verdict.
proposals.rationale: “Now set” is a banned presenter cue. The imperative without the temporal staging preserves the author’s assertive voice.

proposals.old: Now comes the part no skeptic would script.
proposals.new: The next movement is the part no skeptic would invent.
proposals.summary: Remove “Now comes” staging and soft modern “script.”
proposals.rationale: Director open plus film-metaphor “script” both fight house style. The rewrite stays assertive and drops the cue.

proposals.summary: Replace “Listen to” director cue with a direct claim.
proposals.rationale: “Listen to” is a banned presenter cue. A short assertive sentence hands the same structural role to the following evidence.

proposals.old: (The reckoning of those days is the work of _Time Tested Tradition_; mark here only that the sign carries its durations — three days in the fish, three days’ journey in the city, forty days of warning — and that none of them are idle.)
proposals.new: (The reckoning of those days is the work of _Time Tested Tradition_; the sign carries its durations — three days in the fish, three days’ journey in the city, forty days of warning — and none of them are idle.)
proposals.summary: Delete “mark here only that” director cue inside the parenthesis.
proposals.rationale: “Mark here only” is a banned cue. Removing it leaves the factual note clean and still points the reader forward without staging.

proposals.old: See what Jesus says these gentiles will then do: __“The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it.”__
proposals.new: Jesus says these gentiles will then do this: __“The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it.”__
proposals.rationale: “See what” is a banned presenter open. The direct subject-verb form keeps the quotation and the claim.

proposals.old:
But he compressed the whole descent into two frames, and so set one of them wrong: the ship is not the cross.
You have just watched the ship carry the night of the betrayal — the sleeper wakened, the questioning, the innocent blood, the lots — while the cross stands further down, where the reeds are bound about the prophet’s head.
proposals.new:
He compressed the whole descent into two frames, and so set one of them wrong: the ship is not the cross.
The ship carries the night of the betrayal — the sleeper wakened, the questioning, the innocent blood, the lots — while the cross stands further down, where the reeds are bound about the prophet’s head.
proposals.summary: Fix But-open and second-person “You have just watched” staging in one contiguous block.
proposals.rationale: Author prose may not open with But; “You have just watched” is residual director framing. Both fixes restore assertion without altering the Augustine correction or the ship/cross distinction.
